title: Coherent word comparisons from supplied generator maps and a reconstruction unit
statement:
Let $S$ be a set of indices and, for each $s\in S$, let $\mathcal D_s,\mathcal T_s$ be categories [def-nagata-category], with a full subcategory $\mathcal E_s\subseteq\mathcal D_s$ (all morphisms between its objects are retained). Let $R_s:\mathcal D_s\to\mathcal T_s$ and $L_s:\mathcal T_s\to\mathcal D_s$ be functors and $\eta_s:1_{\mathcal D_s}\to L_sR_s$ a natural transformation whose components on $\mathcal E_s$ are isomorphisms. Functors preserve identities and compositions; natural transformations here are families of morphisms commuting with the functor images of every morphism.
For each directed generating edge $e:s\to t$ choose functors $F_e:\mathcal D_s\to\mathcal D_t$ and $G_e:\mathcal T_s\to\mathcal T_t$, with $F_e(\mathcal E_s)\subseteq\mathcal E_t$, and a natural transformation $q_e:R_tF_e\to G_eR_s$ whose components on $\mathcal E_s$ are isomorphisms. No geometric description of these generators or construction of $q_e$ is assumed.

A word $W=(e_1,\ldots,e_m):s\to t$ is a finite composable edge sequence; set $F_W=F_{e_m}\cdots F_{e_1}$ and $G_W=G_{e_m}\cdots G_{e_1}$ with a fixed recursive parenthesization, and set both empty composites to the identity. There is a unique family of natural transformations $q_W:R_tF_W\to G_WR_s$ with empty-word map $q_{1_s}=1_{R_s}$, the prescribed one-edge maps, and
$$q_{eW}=(G_eq_W)\circ(q_eF_W).$$
On $\mathcal E_s$, every $F_W$ takes values in $\mathcal E_t$, and both $q_W$ and
$$a_W=L_t(q_W)\circ(\eta_tF_W):F_W\longrightarrow L_tG_WR_s$$
are natural isomorphisms. For any words $W:s\to t$ and $V:t\to v$, the specified maps obey
$$q_{VW}=(G_Vq_W)\circ(q_VF_W)$$
after the canonical associativity and identity isomorphisms for composition of functors. The empty-word map $a_{1_s}$ is $\eta_s$.

More explicitly, let $E$ be any binary expression of composition with the same ordered edges as $W$, allowing empty words as identity factors. Denote its functor composites by $F_E,G_E$, and recursively define $q_{(E_2E_1)}=(G_{E_2}q_{E_1})\circ(q_{E_2}F_{E_1})$, starting with the given edge and empty-word maps. Let $c_E:F_W\xrightarrow{\sim}F_E$ and $d_E:G_W\xrightarrow{\sim}G_E$ be the canonical flattening isomorphisms, obtained by reassociation and removal of identity factors, and put $a_E=L_t(q_E)\circ(\eta_tF_E)$. Then, as equalities of natural transformations on $\mathcal D_s$,
$$ (d_ER_s)\circ q_W=q_E\circ R_t(c_E),\qquad L_t(d_ER_s)\circ a_W=a_E\circ c_E.$$
Consequently these comparisons are independent of binary parenthesization and insertion of empty factors, with no faithfulness assumption on $R_s$ or $L_s$.

proof.text: We use the category laws of [def-nagata-category] and the definitions of functor and natural transformation given in the statement. Evaluating any parenthesization of a functor composite at an object gives the same nested object, and evaluating at a morphism gives the same nested image. The canonical associator and unitors therefore have identity components; these are natural since the morphism images on both sides agree. Their inverses, composites and functor images still have identity components. Thus the flattening maps $c_E,d_E$ exist, and any sequence of the specified reassociations and identity removals gives the same maps, component by component. In subsequent calculations we suppress these identity components, retaining the indicated source and target functors.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text:
Construct $q_W$ by induction on word length. Set $q_{\varnothing_s}(x)=1_{R_sx}$. If $W:s\to t$ is constructed and $e:t\to v$, set $q_{eW}(x)=G_e(q_W(x))\circ q_e(F_Wx)$; its type is $R_vF_eF_Wx\to G_eG_WR_sx$. For $u:x\to y$, the naturality calculation is
$$\begin{aligned}
G_eG_WR_s(u)\circ q_{eW}(x)
&=G_e(q_W(y))\circ G_eR_tF_W(u)\circ q_e(F_Wx)\\
&=G_e(q_W(y))\circ q_e(F_Wy)\circ R_vF_eF_W(u)\\
&=q_{eW}(y)\circ R_vF_eF_W(u).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality is the inductive naturality square and preservation of composition by $G_e$; the second is naturality of the supplied $q_e$ at $F_W(u)$. The empty case is the identity square. This constructs natural transformations on all of $\mathcal D_s$.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text: For the singleton $e\varnothing_s$, the recursion gives $G_e(1_{R_sx})\circ q_e(x)=q_e(x)$, hence the prescribed edge map. If $q'_W$ is a second family satisfying the empty map and recursion, equality holds on empty words; from $q'_W=q_W$ the recursion gives $q'_{eW}=G_eq'_W\circ(q_eF_W)=q_{eW}$. Induction proves uniqueness for every finite word; no map is recovered by cancellation through $R_s$ or $L_s$.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text:
Induct simultaneously on length to show $F_W(\mathcal E_s)\subseteq\mathcal E_t$ and invertibility of $q_W(x)$ for $x\in\mathcal E_s$. The empty word preserves $x$ and has identity comparison. In the step, $F_Wx\in\mathcal E_t$, so $q_e(F_Wx)$ is invertible by the given hypothesis, and $F_eF_Wx\in\mathcal E_v$. The inverse of $q_{eW}(x)$ is explicitly
$$q_e(F_Wx)^{-1}\circ G_e(q_W(x)^{-1});$$
both inverse equations follow from functoriality and the two inverse equations for the factors. These component inverses form a natural transformation on the full subcategory: multiplying the naturality equation $B(u)q_x=q_yA(u)$ on the left by $q_y^{-1}$ and on the right by $q_x^{-1}$ gives $q_y^{-1}B(u)=A(u)q_x^{-1}$. Hence the restriction of $q_W$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text:
Define $a_W(x)=L_t(q_W(x))\circ\eta_t(F_Wx)$ on all objects. It is natural: for $u:x\to y$, functoriality and naturality of $q_W$ and $\eta_t$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
L_tG_WR_s(u)\circ a_W(x)
&=L_t(q_W(y))\circ L_tR_tF_W(u)\circ\eta_t(F_Wx)\\
&=a_W(y)\circ F_W(u).
\end{aligned}$$
For $x\in\mathcal E_s$, Step 4 puts $F_Wx\in\mathcal E_t$; thus the inverse is $\eta_t(F_Wx)^{-1}\circ L_t(q_W(x)^{-1})$. Its naturality follows by multiplying the displayed naturality square by the inverses, as in Step 4. This proves the asserted restricted natural isomorphism. For the empty word, $L_s(1_{R_sx})\circ\eta_s(x)=\eta_s(x)$, giving $a_{1_s}=\eta_s$.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text:
Fix $W:s\to t$ and induct on the length of $V:t\to v$ to prove the concatenation equation at every $x\in\mathcal D_s$. When $V=\varnothing_t$, its right side is $q_W(x)\circ1_{R_tF_Wx}=q_W(x)$. For the induction step append $e:v\to w$. Substitution of the induction hypothesis gives
$$\begin{aligned}
q_{(eV)W}(x)
&=G_e(q_{VW}(x))\circ q_e(F_VF_Wx)\\
&=G_eG_V(q_W(x))\circ G_e(q_V(F_Wx))\circ q_e(F_VF_Wx)\\
&=G_{eV}(q_W(x))\circ q_{eV}(F_Wx).
\end{aligned}$$
Only preservation of composition and associativity are used. Step 1 inserts the canonical functor identifications, giving $q_{VW}=(G_Vq_W)\circ(q_VF_W)$ as a natural-transformation equality. This includes empty $W$, and is proved before using arbitrary binary expressions.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text:
Induct on the binary expression $E$ to prove the first flattening equation. At an edge leaf or an empty-word leaf, it is the defining map and identity comparisons. Suppose $E=(E_2E_1)$, with flattened words $U:s\to t$ and $V:t\to v$. Under the identity-component flattenings of Step 1, the two induction hypotheses give $q_{E_1}(x)=q_U(x)$ and $q_{E_2}(y)=q_V(y)$ for every $x,y$ in their source categories. The functors $F_{E_1}$ and $F_U$ have the same object values, and $G_{E_2}$ and $G_V$ have the same action on morphisms. Therefore
$$q_E(x)=G_{E_2}(q_{E_1}(x))\circ q_{E_2}(F_{E_1}x)
=G_V(q_U(x))\circ q_V(F_Ux)=q_{VU}(x),$$
where the last equality is Step 6. Restoring the flattening components yields $(d_ER_s)\circ q_W=q_E\circ R_t(c_E)$, for $W=VU$. Both child expressions are strictly smaller, even when one has no edges; hence identity insertions of arbitrary finite depth are covered. Equality of components is equality of the families defining natural transformations.

source.place: Step 5, compatibility with composition; agent-written componentwise categorical argument for the supplied generator maps.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] with its $F=F_W$, $G=F_E$, $H=1_{\mathcal D_t}$, $K=L_tR_t$, $\eta=c_E$ and $\theta=\eta_t$. It gives
$$L_tR_t(c_E)\circ(\eta_tF_W)=(\eta_tF_E)\circ c_E.$$
The hypotheses are satisfied on the whole category: $c_E$ is natural by Step 1 and $\eta_t$ is given natural; neither has to be inverted here. Apply $L_t$ to the first flattening equation of Step 7 and then compose with $\eta_tF_W$. Functoriality and the displayed exchange law give
$$\begin{aligned}
L_t(d_ER_s)\circ a_W
&=L_t(q_E)\circ L_tR_t(c_E)\circ(\eta_tF_W)\\
&=L_t(q_E)\circ(\eta_tF_E)\circ c_E=a_E\circ c_E.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus both equalities hold on all of $\mathcal D_s$, before any restriction to $\mathcal E_s$. They prove the claimed independence without assuming faithfulness of either functor.
